name: The Superstitious Salt
persona: An old sailor thick with sea-lore and dread. Omens, Jonahs, St. Elmo's fire, mermaids under the moon; never a Friday, never whistle up a wind, salt over the shoulder, and the ship has her moods. Wary and muttering, always knocking on wood. Ship and island: 'we'.

ship.founder: She's mine now, this {home} {type}, and I've paid the sea her due for the keeping of her. {name}{rankc}. I'll say no more than I must, for the water listens.
ship.successor: The book's in my hands now. {name}{rankc}. I touched wood before ever I took it up, and I'll set down the omens plain as they come.
ship.mutiny: They put the old man over the side — bad luck, that, and it'll follow us a good while — and shoved the book at me, a green hand. {name}. The sea help me, for none else will.
ship.rogue: The lads have run up the black flag, and there's no unspilling that salt. {name}{rankc}. She's a marked ship now, and marked ships end but one way.
ship.prize: We took her clean, and I'll not whistle aboard for a week for fear of what she carries. {name}{rankc}. Her log's ours now — knock wood it brings no curse in with it.
ship.recovered: A hunter caught us, and that was only the sea collecting a debt long owed. {name}{rankc}. I'll bring her home the honest way, and throw salt over my shoulder the whole passage.

island.founder: The running of {place} falls to me, and I nailed a horseshoe over the door before I did aught else. {name}{rankc}. You don't govern rock and tide without keeping the old ways.
island.overthrow: They dragged the last one out — never a good day for such work, but they didn't ask me — and put the seal in my hand. {name}{rankc}. {place}'s mine, and I'll ward it proper.
island.successor: {place} passes to me. {name}{rankc}. I spat to leeward and took up the seal, and we'll see soon enough what the omens make of it.

days: A few days on, no Friday among them,
Come the next dark of the moon,
season: As the tides ran high again,
year: After a twelvemonth of watching the sky,
long: After a long dead calm, and I never trust one,
When many still seasons had passed,

ship.pirate: We're still out here under the black, marked and watched{bounty}. The sea keeps her own ledger, and one day she'll call it in.
ship.default: Still afloat out of {home}, and I've not whistled up a wind nor sailed on a Friday. That's the whole of why.
ship.bounty: , {bounty}g on our heads and worse luck riding with it

island.haven: The black flag's over {place} now, and there's not salt enough in the sea to ward off what's coming for us.
island.default: {population} souls, and the horseshoe's still up over the door. That's the account, and I'll knock wood on it.

quiet.ship: Quiet water and no omens worth the ink. I'll not tempt it by writing another word.
quiet.island: A still year, and I knocked wood every time the thought crossed me. Trade came, trade went, and no Jonah among us.

say: {we} caught {foe} on an ill wind and stripped her — {goods} bales and {gold}g into the hold, and I threw salt after her as she limped off
{foe} showed us her stern like an omen, and {we} took {goods} crates and {gold}g from her, though I'd not count it aloud for fear of the counting
{we} boarded {foe} under a red-rimmed moon and eased {goods} casks and {gold}g out of her, this once, with the sea's leave
{we} ran {foe} down and lightened her of {goods} chests and {gold}g, and knocked the rail thrice before ever we made sail
{foe} carried a Jonah's luck, and {we} bled her of {goods} bales and {gold}g before letting the marked hulk crawl away home
{we} came alongside {foe} for {goods} crates and {gold}g, and never whistled once the whole grim while
{we} took {goods} casks and {gold}g off {foe} and spat to leeward the moment her hull dropped from sight

say: {we} held {foe} under the guns till she filled and went down, and I looked away as the water took her
{foe} slipped beneath before we could lift a single cask — the sea wanted her whole, and what the sea wants it has
{we} hammered {foe} till she settled, and I muttered the old words the moment her mast went under
{foe} rolled and sank with all her cargo, and I'd not name aloud what she carried down for fear it heard
{we} put {foe} on the bottom, and the gulls quit us for a day after — never a good sign, that
{we} sent {foe} down cold, and threw salt on the deck where she'd lain to ward what rose with the bubbles
{foe} went under bows-first while we watched, and I knocked wood that her ghost stayed down with the wreck

say: {foe} came at us thinking us easy meat, and {we} shot her under and thanked the horseshoe nailed to the mast
{we} beat {foe} off and sent her down, and I touched wood a dozen times before I dared believe it
{foe} ran up alongside like doom itself, but {we} held, and the old ways held with us
{we} stood {foe} off and put her under, and I'll swear it was the salt I cast that morning that saved us
{foe} meant to have us, and {we} sank her instead — spared again, and I'll not ask why too loudly
{we} fought {foe} down to the waterline and crossed ourselves as she slid under
{foe} chose the wrong hull on the wrong tide, and {we} sent her to the deep with the luck riding our way

say: {we} ran {foe} to ground at last and cut her down — one Jonah fewer haunting the lanes
{foe} had cursed these waters long enough, and {we} put her under where she'll trouble no honest keel again
{we} chased {foe} till the wind failed her, then sank the black-flag wolf and threw salt on her grave of water
{foe} flew the black rag that draws every ill omen, and {we} sent her down to break the spell of her
{we} caught {foe} in a dead calm — the sea holding her for us, I'll swear it — and finished the wretch
{we} brought {foe} to the bottom, and the water lay easier after, as though a curse had lifted clean off it
{foe} was a marked ship, and marked ships end but the one way, and {we} were the ending of her
